source.revision: main plus the release pull request for build maverick-public-dev-20261125.1 (Waydroid helper, polkit and udev rules, sound report, release notes, rights review, changelog, readme, manifest)
source.dirty_delta: The build ran from builder/public-image/rootfs-overlay/ and build-root.sh with content identical to the files in main after the dev.8 pull request (the changed overlay files are usr/local/sbin/fz-waydroid (new), usr/local/sbin/fz-sound-setup, etc/udev/rules.d/90-froodzos-internal-ro.rules and etc/polkit-1/rules.d/90-froodzos-mount-internal.rules (new)). The boot images are the dev.7 files, unchanged.
source.note: The root is derived from the pinned Phase 1 root (sha256 22dde19c5a9e0b2a6e00f30cce7d0866d08159e1127871793553cd0478d1aacf) by builder/public-image/build-root.sh, built in eight steps (r10 = the dev.3 root; r11 adds PKGS="pipewire-audio pipewire-pulse plasma-pa libgpiod" and the sound overlay; r12 adds pipewire-alsa and the shutdown drop-ins; r13 adds the fz-bootmnt-ro service; r14 to r16 add fz-sound-setup and its unit and launcher, the read-only internal-drive udev rule and the dev.5 version strings; r17 starts the sound set-up from a timer, fixes its --dry-run, adds fz-swap-lr and the dev.6 version strings; r18 replaces the udev read-only rule with one that runs blockdev --setro, updates fz-dtb-fixup.py and sets the dev.7 version strings; r19 adds waydroid, lxc, dnsmasq, libgbinder and python-gbinder with their dependencies (PKGS), the fz-waydroid helper, the sound channel report and a udev rule that shows the internal disk without mounting it; r20 adds the polkit rule for the read-only mount and sets the dev.8 version strings), each a full system upgrade with PRUNE=1, the overlay files, a prebuilt ld.so.cache and size reduction.

inputs.uki_change: The first two boot entries use froodzos-maverick-dspN2.efi: the dev.4 sound boot image with a device-tree change made by fz-dtb-fixup.py --enable-nvme (internal NVMe PCIe controller and PHY enabled; the wake-gpios property of the controller node deleted because its root-port child repeats it). The third entry keeps the touchpad boot image, which does not enable the internal disk.
inputs.menu: output/grub.cfg.public15 (sha256 bd0ae003f643ec030a4788f00054ab4b40ac57912a3a28b804532887547400b5) generated from the dev.7 menu (grub.cfg.public14) by changing the version text; three boot entries and a firmware entry, no submenu, no chain-loading; kernel options include kestrel_graphics_unbounded=1, sysctl.kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0, cow_spacesize=2G; no fz_autorun, fz_persist, fz_dsp or fz_tplg (the second entry adds fz_sound=1)
inputs.root_package_origin: 794 pacman packages (all unmodified Arch Linux ARM except the one project-built kernel); plus two unmodified upstream release tarballs (Helium, Zen) listed in pkglist.tsv
other_removals: usr/lib/firmware/updates (vendor firmware extracted from a Windows installation)
pacman keyring private key and revocation certificate
project-local overlay repository and its signature
four Arch Linux logo files (usr/share/pixmaps/archlinux-logo*) and the LOGO reference
firmware for other Qualcomm chip families and older Wi-Fi generations
development headers, introspection and cmake files

toolchain.squashfs: mksquashfs from squashfs-tools 4.7.5, xz, 128 KiB blocks (build-root.sh)
toolchain.grub: Arch Linux ARM package grub 2:2.16-1 (grub-mkstandalone, arm64-efi)
toolchain.uki: stubblify with the pinned stubble stub (ubuntu/stubble 9f11278e080a5c4a77db6acf4c8f75c14412087a)

board_profile.firmware: none of the vendor 83N3 firmware is included; Arch Linux ARM linux-firmware-qcom (X1E80100/X1P42100 and video decoder files only after pruning), -atheros (ath12k only after pruning), -realtek and licence texts are included
board_profile.redistribution_status: reviewed 2026-11-11, see RIGHTS-REVIEW.md; ALARM publishes no explicit redistribution statement (accepted risk); GPL written offer in SOURCE-OFFER.md

test_receipts.name: file-listing comparison of this root against the dev.7 root (r18)
test_receipts.result: 114300 entries in the new root against 113758 in the dev.7 root: 0 removed / 542 added / 433 changed (the Waydroid stack: waydroid, lxc, dnsmasq, libgbinder, libglibutil, python-gbinder, python-dbus, python-gobject, gobject-introspection-runtime, libgirepository, rsync and wget with their libraries, apparmor profile files for lxc, package database entries, group/passwd/shadow entries of the new packages, ld.so.cache, and the files of this build: fz-waydroid, fz-sound-setup, the udev rule and the polkit rule); 794 packages (782 in dev.7 plus 12); no vendor firmware, no Firefox, no Arch logo, no private key in the added entries; the android system image is not in the root

test_receipts.name: QEMU boot of this release image
test_receipts.result: passed in 336.5 s with an emulated NVMe disk and the Waydroid checks: multi-user reached, login and commands ran, build id maverick-public-dev-20261125.1, kernel package linux-froodzos-arm64, no firefox, no Arch logo files, handlers installed, fz-smartlog running, selftest pass, no vendor firmware directory, no private keyring key, no panic; NVMe markers: read-only flag on the disk and all partitions, write refused, device not auto-mounted (UDISKS_AUTO=0, no UDISKS_IGNORE, ro,nosuid,nodev,noexec mount options); Waydroid markers: binder_linux loads and the binder filesystem appears, waydroid, lxc-start, dnsmasq and nft present, fz-waydroid init refuses without a persistent partition
test_receipts.scope: emulator (QEMU TCG virt) with grub.cfg replaced by a test variant, with an emulated 64 MB NVMe disk with two partitions (FZ_NVME=1) and the Waydroid checks (FZ_WAYDROID=1); image sha256 1c95d7b221b859cee2c74bcc74de7fc06be02f34f60c6ec3c9c3e4bf8cefd41f; not laptop hardware

test_receipts.name: native boots of a private test stick on the Lenovo 83N3 (owner, 2026-11-25), previous test root r19
test_receipts.result: the owner booted the dev.7 boot image dspN2 with the test root r19 (the same Waydroid package set, fz-waydroid helper, sound channel report and the udev rule that shows the internal disk without mounting it as this release; r19 lacks only the polkit rule and the dev.8 version strings) from a private test stick with fz_sound=1 and fz_persist=1 (a 32 GB ext4 FROODZ_PERSIST partition on the stick; the stick menu used a 3 GB RAM overlay). Results: desktop started, no kernel oops, Wi-Fi and sound worked, fz-waydroid check reported READY, fz-waydroid init downloaded the Android 13 image (about 1 GB) onto the persistent partition, Android booted completely (sys.boot_completed=1, about 16 s) and its window was displayed after enabling the Waydroid multi-window property; the internal disk showed read-only flag 1 on the disk and all partitions. The Android cgroup warnings were non-fatal. Dolphin asked for an administrator password when the internal Windows partition was clicked: this is why the polkit rule was added; the passwordless mount was NOT tested on the laptop before this release. The released image itself was not written to a stick and booted
test_receipts.scope: owner test on one laptop; private menu; the root of this release (r20, sha256 above) and the released image were not themselves booted on the laptop at the time of the build; Android rendering is software only

limitations: Sound needs the owner's own audio firmware: the image contains none. fz-sound-setup reads it from the owner's Windows partition on the internal disk (mounted read-only; not possible if Windows is BitLocker-encrypted) or from a FroodzOS-firmware folder on the stick, copies six files into memory and restarts the audio DSP (command, or the second boot entry, which starts it about 75 seconds after boot). Left and right can come out reversed on some boots (cause not found; fz-swap-lr swaps them).
Graphics are software-rendered (llvmpipe) on a firmware framebuffer; there is no GPU acceleration. USB-C display output and alternate modes are not claimed.
Touchpad: the kernel driver binds and the pad works in an owner test; gesture quality is unconfirmed. The second boot entry keeps the user-space polling driver.
Battery level, charge state and USB-C power data work in an owner test; power management beyond that is not claimed.
Wi-Fi does not recover after suspend and resume; suspend and resume are not claimed. A memory-bandwidth monitor driver (bwmon) fails to load its table.
RAR is extract-only (UnRAR licence). Wine, Waydroid and QEMU are not included.
Helium and Zen are unmodified third-party releases; their trademark and artwork terms were not reviewed separately and the Helium signing key is not otherwise certified.
Browser sandboxes need unprivileged user namespaces; the image sets kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0.
Boot loader and kernel images are unsigned; Secure Boot must be off. The downloads are signed (SHA256SUMS.asc).
Opt-in persistence (fz_persist=1) was tested on hardware only on the private stick; whoever holds the stick can read what is stored on the persistent partition.
No vendor firmware is included. Default live accounts are those of the development image (user live, password live).
Arch Linux ARM publishes no explicit redistribution statement; the maintainer acceptance of the three-year written source offer is recorded at release approval.

The internal disk is visible to the live system and, since dev.8, in the desktop file manager. It is flagged read-only by a udev rule when it appears (blockdev --setro on the disk and every partition), is never mounted automatically (UDISKS_AUTO=0) and a mount by the user is forced to ro,nosuid,nodev,noexec; a polkit rule lets the local active session do that mount without a password. There is a short moment before the flag is set. The polkit rule is not tested on the laptop. The cause of the dev.5 kernel crash with an enabled PCIe controller is not proven.

Waydroid is experimental: the Android image is not part of the release, it is downloaded by the user (about 1 GB) onto the persistent partition by fz-waydroid init (the released image has no such partition; fz-waydroid init --ram keeps it in memory); no GPU acceleration, no Google Play, camera and sensors untested; the window may need the multi-window property. Wine is not included (not in the Arch Linux ARM repositories).

The release image itself was only emulator-tested; the owner tests used the identical boot images and a previous test root with the same Waydroid, sound and udev content on a private stick, with the second-entry kernel options.
